Theme 091 · Art movements & eras

Beveled '95 Desktop

Mid-90s desktop nostalgia: a teal desktop, grey bevelled windows, cascading spreadsheets, modal dialogs and a taskbar with a clock. It turns dashboard fatigue into a very literal pile of windows, lets Pulse arrive as a splash screen, stages the anomaly as the one dialog you actually want to see — and the Start button finally says "Start free".

COMPONENT KIT

  • Bevelled window — grey #C6C6C6 frame with 4-tone inset bevel and teal gradient title bar
  • Cascade stack — dashboard_33…38.xls windows offset 34 px — the dashboard pile
  • Modal dialog — warning / alert box with icon, message and a focused default button
  • Splash screen — bevelled panel with the Acme mark and version line
  • Taskbar & tray — clock and tray icon; the tray hosts Pulse in the background
  • Start menu — vertical brand band + coloured items; the Start button reads Start free

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Cascade spawn — each window appears instantly (no easing) with a 2-frame outline zoom, one per 8th note — authentic and rhythmic
  • Minimise-all — windows scale 1→0 toward their taskbar slots, power2.in 0.25 s, all on the drop
  • Cursor glide & click — cursor moves along a slight arc, power1.inOut 0.75 s, button bevel inverts for 2 frames exactly on the beat

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Everybody who buys software has fought a pile of windows; the '95 metaphor makes the pain funny and makes Pulse's 'background tray agent' role literal. The teal desktop is already Acme's colour. Risk: nostalgia can read as dated or as a parody of a specific OS — keep it generic (no real logos, sounds or product names).

Adapt to your product: Rebuild your real UI screenshots inside bevelled windows, cast your product's key notification as the modal dialog, and relabel the Start button with your CTA.

References: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_95 — mid-90s desktop UI conventions: taskbar, Start button, bevelled 3D widgets · https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare — Susan Kare: pixel icons and early GUI visual language
